arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9 two-player, reply-search root256/slate8/opponent64, action limit1000, completed turns sampled at round modulo4 equals0

shared_model.features: Same frozen spatial features plus17 root material/static features
shared_model.head: Same seeded two-layer128 ReLU scorer,20 epochs,map-balanced SmoothL1 relative-to-static pairs
shared_model.target: asinh(native searched-opponent reply score/1000); same candidate labels in both arms
shared_model.use_at_inference: Neither head is a deployable agent; post-reply state is an offline oracle for this information-boundary diagnostic

interpretation: Giving the frozen-feature scorer the actual successor state after the searched opponent full turn improves rare beneficial-pair detection from58 to103 on identical fresh-map candidates, so response-state information is useful. It does not solve selection: even with that offline oracle input, the selected candidate has a worse native reply score than static rank zero at80 positions versus37 better, and independent maps favor static19 versus6. The relative MAE is slightly worse after the reply. This rejects both diagnostic heads as policies and shows that opponent transition prediction is not the sole observed bottleneck for this frozen representation/objective. Correlated candidates and32 validation maps limit causal interpretation. No terminal-game, Elo or deployment claim follows.
